overview: Cross-sectional last-shift survey of registered and licensed practical nurses on 18 adult inpatient units over four weeks in January and February 2027, completed during 20 minutes of paid time, with each response linked to the planned and actual hours and the acuity of the unit on the shift described.
population: All registered and licensed practical nurses who worked at least one shift on one of the 18 units in the survey window; agency staff excluded because they cannot be given paid time.
exposure: Shift staffing ratio: actual divided by planned nursing hours for the unit and shift described, from the scheduling system; below plan means at least 10 percent below. Patients per nurse on that shift is a secondary exposure.
procedures: The checklist is adapted from a 22-item last-shift instrument and pretested with eight licensed practical nurses and four registered nurses. Nurses complete it on a tablet during paid time on any shift, naming the unit, date and shift type of their last shift. The analyst links each response to the scheduling system and to the mean morning acuity score of that unit on that date, then deletes the date, keeping only the linked variables.

outcomes.name: Any missed care on the last shift
outcomes.measure: At least one of 22 activities reported as missed
outcomes.timing: Last shift worked, reported within 72 hours
outcomes.why: The measure both management and the union asked for; directly tied to patient care.

outcomes.name: Number of activities missed
outcomes.measure: Count of the 22 activities reported as missed
outcomes.why: Shows the amount as well as the presence of missed care.

outcomes.name: Missed or late timed medicines
outcomes.measure: Yes or no item on the checklist

outcomes.name: Response by unit, role and shift type
outcomes.why: Differential response by night and part-time staff is the main threat.

feasibility: About 1,150 eligible nurses; 20 minutes of paid time each for about 575 expected responses is about 190 nursing hours, within the union agreement; linkage uses existing extracts.
biasMitigation: Last-shift recall rather than a longer period
Staffing taken from the scheduling system, not from the nurse
Acuity measured for the same unit and date
Reporting cells of five or more responses only

biasFlags.label: Nonresponse by shift and role
biasFlags.note: Paid time on every shift type limits it; response is reported by role and shift.

biasFlags.label: Acuity measured as a unit mean
biasFlags.note: May not reflect the nurse's own patients.

biasFlags.label: Reporting bias from the survey's purpose
biasFlags.note: Both sides have an interest in the result; the checklist wording and reporting rule are agreed with both before fielding.

flags: Five adjustment variables fixed in advance
parsimony.simplestPath: One survey window, one primary outcome, one staffing exposure, one acuity adjustment.

theoreticalFramework: No framework beyond the survey design; SEIPS is used only to name work-system factors in the reasons section.
summary: Four-week linked last-shift survey with one primary outcome and response tracked by role and shift.
